 Bayern Munich’s Max Eberl expecting ‘complicated’ challenge from Atlético Madrid
 FC Bayern is going to have a battle on its hands.
 by CSmith1919 Updated Nov 3, 2026, 7:00 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 (Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images) Getty Images Part Of Atlético Madrid vs. Bayern Munich: 2026/27 Champions League full coverage see all updates CSmith1919 Chuck Smith is the site manager for Bavarian Football Works, where he began writing in 2017. He is the author of The Daily Schmankerl, the longest-running daily Bayern Munich column in English, and also writes The Weekend Warm-Up. In addition to covering Bayern Munich news and providing commentary on Bayern Munich, the Bundesliga, and the German national team. He brings more than 30 years of sports-writing experience to the site. Over the course of his career, he has written for numerous newspapers and websites. Bayern Munich sporting director Max Eberl knows exactly what awaits his team in Madrid. Ahead of tomorrow’s Champions League showdown against Atlético Madrid, Eberl has acknowledged the enormous challenge facing Vincent Kompany’s injury-hit squad.
 Atlético are among the most difficult opponents Bayern could encounter away from home, particularly at the Metropolitano, where Diego Simeone’s side will look to make life uncomfortable from the opening whistle.
 Eberl believes Bayern will need to demonstrate the same resilience they have been forced to show throughout a difficult stretch of the season.
 ”It’s definitely one of the most complicated away games you can have in the Champions League, against an extremely difficult and high-quality opponent, where we have to bring the resilience we’ve had to show in recent weeks onto the pitch. It’s a team that will really challenge us a lot. We’re still going there to try and achieve the best possible result,” Eberl said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ).
 There is certainly no shortage of obstacles for Bayern. The injuries to Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari have further depleted the available options, while Jamal Musiala and Luis Díaz are still working toward their returns.
 Nevertheless, Bayern are not traveling to Madrid simply to survive 90 minutes. Two consecutive Champions League draws have made this an important opportunity to get their European campaign moving in the right direction.
 Eberl understands the difficulty of the assignment, but the ambition remains clear: Bayern want a result. Now they have to go out and earn it.
